$comment: Desk grade (not hands-on). Steam review quotes from the English review JSON (filter=all, 70 unique reviews sampled, 59% up); review ids given.
game: Idle Champions of the Forgotten Realms
build: Steam app 627690 as of 2026-10-15 (latest Steam news 2026-10-08 'Liar's Night is here with Kitiara!'; 140+ Champions)

package.basis: desk: Steam store data and review API (9,570 English reviews, 76% positive, Mostly Positive), the Idle Champions fandom wiki (Familiars, Modron Core), Steam discussions, platform listings and prior repo research; not played.

fun.source: desk estimate: formation strategy and the D&D cast give real decisions, but reviews describe resets as work ('you've successfully made work') and offline as weak; placed between the mediocre idle RPG composite (30.8) and Melvor (65.4, eval/calibration/melvor-idle.scorecard.json)

evidence.quote: unites iconic Champions from D&D TRPG campaigns, video games, novels, actual plays, comic books, and shows
a huge cast of well-known Dungeons & Dragons characters

dims.note: Licensed cast drawn in one cartoon register, small sprites on busy backgrounds; reviews praise the cast more than the art. Matches the 50 anchor.

evidence.quote: Even with all graphical features turned off, this relatively simple 2D idle game can become surprisingly resource-hungry

dims.note: Sprite attack loops and ultimates; few review comments on animation. Low confidence.

evidence.quote: the user interface is mediocre on a large monitor
Too many things interrupt the gameplay.
When I open it I am bombarded with at least 5 pop-ups asking for money.

dims.note: Store pop-ups and modal interruptions on top of dense formation/specialization screens.

evidence.quote: The highlight of the game is the in-game juke box. The music is D&D themed and a lot of fun.
listening to the same song over and over gets boring over time

dims.note: Graded from review quotes, not listened. Pleasant themed music with repetition fatigue.

evidence.quote: the brand new Bastion hub to show all the features. I tried onboarding without it and it was rather confusing.
They get unlocked after having reached area 66 in any campaign.
a total of three Modron Cores through the completion of the Split The Party adventures

dims.note: Core act (level champions, place formation) is immediate; automation is gated (familiars at area 66, Modron after Split the Party, a week or more per prior research). A new hub helps.

evidence.quote: Eventually, leveling up takes hours, so you have to restart, get a little more money the next time
Every week there's a lot you have to do
Difficulty creep over time isn't fun or engaging.

dims.note: Adventure resets feel alike; events every few weeks add champions but also obligations. No ending.

evidence.quote: There's a ton of nuance when it comes to building teams in different formations and what abilities to use.
it can be hard to keep up with the meta
Optimize formations using over 140 Champions, each with unique abilities

dims.note: Positional synergy and per-adventure restrictions change the best formation (above the 50 anchor), but a community meta per variant rules.

evidence.quote: can be purchased with either real money, gems, Patron shops, and Seasons rewards that allow the player to automate clicking and leveling up Champions
An idle game that demands to be running 24/7 because offline resource gains are abyssmal
There are an enormous number of ways to spend money on very small additions or conveniences.

dims.note: Paid automation (familiars ~$6 each per review 235884423), weak offline (background parties cut, steamcommunity.com/app/627690/discussions/0/3770112515482301845 via prior research). Matches the ~20 anchor. No direct real-money purchase of a created timer found (time gate pieces come from patron currency), so the kill is not set.

evidence.quote: to watch my group of heroes either struggle to survive or finally be[at]
Idle Champions (gold rain, ultimates)

dims.note: Gold rain and ultimates; chest opening called work (review 231953911: 'Somehow even opening chests is work'). Low confidence.

evidence.quote: it is notoriously buggy and the framerates at times can be abysmal
Over longer sessions, it seems to consume more and more resources and can eventually crash.
it tends to crash my computer

dims.note: Six years of weekly patches; resource leaks and bugs are a recurring cluster.

evidence.quote: over 140 Champions ... countless monsters across hundreds of adventures
new champions coming out every other week or so on rotation with events

dims.note: Huge roster and adventure list; many adventures are variants of the same campaign maps.

evidence.quote: an official Dungeons & Dragons® idle clicker game
This game is like gardening. You tend the adventure party

dims.note: The license is the twist; mechanically a Crusaders-of-the-Lost-Idols-style formation clicker.

evidence.quote: PC Windows, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Android, Apple iOS listed
Windows, Mac; 7 languages; Remote Play on Tablet
Not possible to transfer between platforms (player thread, 2021)

dims.note: Wide platform reach (also Switch, destructoid.com/?p=257847) but no cross-progress found; no text/motion settings evidence.

learn.practice: Positional formation synergy: where a unit stands changes what its abilities do, so one roster gives many builds per restriction.
learn.evidence: https://idlechampions.fandom.com/wiki/Idle_Champions_of_the_Forgotten_Realms — 'Mastering the position of each Champion to maximize their special abilities is the key to completing each adventure.'

learn.practice: An earned automation core that saves a formation and runs resets for the player (the Modron), unlocked by play rather than sold.
learn.evidence: https://idlechampions.fandom.com/wiki/Modron_Core — 'Modron Core is required to use the Modron Automation ... through the completion of the Split The Party adventures'

learn.practice: A jukebox the player controls: letting players pick tracks counters loop fatigue cheaply.
learn.evidence: https://store.steampowered.com/appreviews/627690 (review 235101834) — 'The highlight of the game is the in-game juke box.'

learn.practice: Anti-pattern: paid automation plus weak offline turns an idler into a job; keep automation earned and absence rewarded.
learn.evidence: https://store.steampowered.com/appreviews/627690 (review 231953911) — 'For the developers, you've successfully made work.'
